title: Rounding the Fixed Monthly Sum of a Standing Automatic Payment, by Certificate Relationship
content:
How the figure obtained for a fixed monthly sum on a card under Personal Credit Cards is rounded is read from the cardholder's holdings under Certificates of Deposit.

| What the certificate records show | How the figure is rounded |
|---|---|
| An active certificate whose principal balance is at least 10000.00 USD, and at least 1 certificate interest payout posted to the cardholder's certificates in the last six months | rounded half-up to the nearest whole dollar |
| An active certificate whose principal balance is below 10000.00 USD, and at least 1 certificate interest payout posted to the cardholder's certificates in the last six months | reduced to the whole dollar below it |
| Neither of those | rounded half-up to the cent |

**Both parts of each row.** An active certificate of the stated principal and at least 1 certificate interest payout in the last six months are required together. A cardholder holding an active certificate of 50000.00 USD whose certificates paid out no interest in the last six months falls in the third row, and so does a cardholder whose certificate matured and closed before the payout window was reached.

**Worked on hypothetical figures.** A figure of 899.685 becomes 900.00 USD under the first convention, 899.00 USD under the second and 899.69 USD under the third. A figure of 315.50 becomes 316.00 USD, 315.00 USD and 315.50 USD respectively. A principal balance of exactly 10000.00 USD belongs to the first row, the test being at least that amount.
